title: Minimum Number of Taps to Open to Water a Garden
summary: Given a garden on the x-axis from 0 to n, with taps at each integer point, and each tap having a watering range defined by an array, determine the minimum number of taps needed to water the entire garden.
statement: Given a garden on the x-axis from 0 to n, with taps at each integer point, and each tap having a watering range defined by an array, determine the minimum number of taps needed to water the entire garden. If it's impossible, return -1.
constraints: The garden is the continuous segment from zero through n.
Tap i waters [i-ranges[i], i+ranges[i]], clipped to the garden.
Return the fewest taps covering every point, or -1 if a gap cannot be covered.
hints: Convert taps into intervals grouped by their left endpoint.
Scan like minimum jumps, tracking the farthest point reachable by one more selected interval.
When the current chosen coverage ends, commit the interval reaching farthest; fail if it does not advance.
The exchange rule can replace any next interval by the farthest-reaching available interval without using more taps.
editorial: Compress all intervals starting at the same left position to their farthest right endpoint. A frontier scan greedily commits only when current coverage expires, choosing the farthest endpoint seen so far. This is the standard minimum interval-cover exchange argument. The independent oracle enumerates tap subsets on seeded small gardens and checks their sorted union.

tests.explanation: The tap at position one alone covers the entire garden.
No tap reaches beyond its own point, leaving every open interval dry.
